summary: Clare Carlisle is a scholar in philosophy and religious studies who studied at Trinity College, Cambridge (1995–2002). She served as Lecturer in Philosophy at the University of Liverpool (~2006–2011) and became a professor at King's College London (~2011).

Linguist Claude Hagège studied at institutions including École Normale Supérieure, École des langues orientales, and under André Martinet at Paris Descartes University. His appointments include CNRS, University of Poitiers, École Pratique des Hautes Études, and Collège de France (1988–2006).

Claude Jacques was an indologist and historian who studied under George Cœdès. He taught epigraphy and history at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1970–1998) and served as director of the École Française d'Extrême-Orient (~1989–1992).

Claude Lévi-Strauss studied at the Paris Law Faculty and under Marcel Mauss. He worked in philosophy and other fields, holding positions at the University of São Paulo, EPHE, EHESS, and the Collège de France as chair of Anthropologie sociale (1959–1982).

Claude-Auguste Court was active in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at the École polytechnique (~1810–1812) and the École Spéciale Militaire de Saint-Cyr (~1812–1813), later serving as an Engineer Officer in the Sikh Khalsa Army (~1827–1843).
Claudia Benthien works in linguistics and other fields. She studied at Washington University in St. Louis (1993–1994) and held a post at the University of Hamburg (~2005).
Claudia Weber is a scholar in Indology and religious studies. She studied under Hans-Joachim Klimkeit as her teacher and Gregor Ahn as her project supervisor.

Claudius Buchanan was an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Glasgow, the University of Cambridge, and Queens' College, Cambridge. In 1801, he served as Vice-Provost at Fort William College.

Claus Oetke, an Indologist and philosopher, completed his PhD and habilitation at the University of Hamburg, where he was a Dozent (~1973–1988). He later headed the Department of Indology at Stockholm University (1993–2014).

Indologist and tibetologist Claus Vogel completed his PhD and habilitation at the University of Marburg, where he also held posts. He later taught at the University of Göttingen and served as Ordinarius at the University of Bonn (1976–1998).
Clemency Montelle is a scholar in Indology and history/archaeology who has held posts at the University of Canterbury in 2007 and from 2020 to 2025.
Linguist Clemente Merlo studied at the University of Pavia from ~1898 to 1902. He subsequently held a post at the University of Pisa from ~1908 to 1949.
Clyde Kluckhohn studied at Princeton, Wisconsin-Madison, Oxford, Vienna, and Harvard. He held academic posts at the University of New Mexico (~1932–1934) and Harvard University (~1935–1960).

Colette Caillat was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Louis Renou, Jules Bloch, and Walther Schubring. She held posts at CNRS, the University of Lyon, Sorbonne University (1967–1988), and directed the Institut de civilisation indienne (~1978–1990).

Colette Sciberras works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. She studied at Durham University, where she was supervised by David E. Cooper and Simon P. James, and also studied under traditional teachers Yungdrung Nyima and Chamtrul Rinpoche.
Colin Leslie Dean is a scholar in philosophy and religious studies who studied under supervisors Peter Fenner and Purushottama Bilimoria (attested 2002).
Colin Turnbull worked in Tibetology and other fields. He studied at Westminster School (~1938–1942), Magdalen College (~1942–1947), and Banaras Hindu University (~1949–1951).

Collett Cox, a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, earned a PhD from Columbia University under Alex Wayman and Yoshito S. Hakeda and studied in Japan. She served as a professor at the University of Washington (attested 1999, 2017).

Conor Roddy works in philosophy and Indology. He earned a PhD from the University of Texas at Austin under Kathleen M. Higgins (attested 2011) and was taught by William Lyons, Arindam Chakrabarti, Graham Parkes, and Roger T. Ames.

Conrad Bursian was a scholar of history and archaeology who studied at Thomasschule, Leipzig University, and Berlin. He held posts at Leipzig, the University of Tübingen, the University of Zurich, the University of Jena, and the University of Munich (~1874–1883).
